title: Clearly we have not been holding enough space for the lyrics of Defyi...
transcript: I think that we forget, like, what a huge cultural phenomenon Glee was when it came out, because, like, what do you mean that the Glee version of Defying Gravity out charted the movie version of Defying Gravity? Like, maybe it's just me living in my little musical theater bubble, but I feel like this song has been everywhere. Like, we have been holding space. And yet the Glee cover from, like, 15 years ago out charted it. And to be fair, I remember this being a big deal at the time because up until that point, they really hadn't done any modern musical theater. And so the fact that they were doing wicked on Glee was, like, a huge deal. And this was Glee in its prime. Like, season 1, episode 9. Everyone was obsessed. This was, like, also around the time that everyone was dream casting Lea Michele in the wicked movie, and there were, like, rumors that she was gonna do it, even though we all know that her version is not the best version of Defying Gravity. It is, in fact, the Amber Riley version. But anyway, I'm going on a Tangent. The point is, this is a crazy stat and also a hilarious one.
